services.name: Roadside Assistance
services.short: When your truck or trailer stops, we come to you. Call, share your location, and we'll get a technician rolling.
services.title: Truck & Trailer Roadside Assistance, Garland TX
services.description: Broken down? Sunny Side sends help for flat tires, dead batteries, air and electrical problems and more across the Dallas–Fort Worth area.

services.name: Brakes & Air Systems
services.short: Inspection, adjustment and repair for air brakes, from slack adjusters and drums to compressors and air dryers.
services.title: Truck Brake & Air System Repair in Garland, TX
services.description: Air brake inspection, adjustment and repair for tractors, straight trucks and trailers: slack adjusters, drums, chambers, compressors, air dryers and ABS faults.
services.lead: Brakes are the one system you never want to guess about. We inspect, adjust and repair air brake systems on tractors, straight trucks and trailers.
intro: Air brake systems have a lot of moving parts, and every one of them wears. We check the whole system rather than just the pads and drums, so small problems get caught before they put you out of service.
You'll get a plain-language rundown of what we found, what needs attention now, and what can wait.
included: Brake inspection and adjustment, including slack adjusters
Brake shoes, drums, pads and rotors
Air compressor and air dryer service
ABS diagnosis and wheel-speed sensor replacement
Spring brake and parking brake repair
Brake-related wheel-end work such as seals and bearings
signs: Air hissing when the truck sits or when you apply the brakes
Slow air pressure build-up
The low-air warning light or buzzer comes on
Pulling to one side when braking
Longer stopping distance or a soft pedal feel
Grinding, squealing or a burning smell from a wheel

steps.d: We check the full system, measure wear and test for air leaks.
We walk you through what we found and give you a clear estimate.
After your approval we fix it, adjust the brakes and road-test the result.

faqs.q: What does the low-air warning mean?
faqs.a: Federal rules require a warning signal when air pressure in the service reservoir drops to 55 psi or below (49 CFR 393.51). If it comes on, find a safe place to stop and call for help rather than pushing on.

faqs.q: Can you fix an air leak on the road?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Many leaks come from hoses, fittings or chambers that can be repaired on site. See our roadside assistance page.

faqs.q: How often should brakes be inspected?
faqs.a: Brakes are checked at every DOT annual inspection. Good practice is to look at them at every preventive maintenance visit and during your pre-trip inspection, too.

services.name: Engine & Aftertreatment Diagnostics
services.short: Fault-code diagnosis and repair for diesel engines, including DPF, DEF, SCR and EGR systems.
services.title: Diesel Engine & DPF/DEF/EGR Repair, Garland TX
services.description: Diesel engine diagnostics and repair for trucks: check-engine lights, derates, DPF, DEF, SCR, EGR, turbo and cooling problems traced to the cause.
services.lead: A warning light or a derate doesn't have to mean a guessing game. We trace diesel engine and aftertreatment problems to the cause, not just the code.
intro: Modern diesel engines are a system of sensors, software and emissions equipment. A fault code tells you where to look; it doesn't tell you what failed. We confirm the cause with testing before we recommend parts.
That means fewer return trips and fewer parts swapped on a hunch.
included: Fuel system service: filters, lift pump and injectors
Cooling system repair: radiator, water pump, thermostat and hoses
signs: The check-engine or stop-engine light is on
The engine goes into a derate and loses power
Frequent regeneration warnings
Hard starting or rough running
Heavy smoke, a coolant smell or oil leaks
Temperature climbing on a hill or in traffic

steps.d: We read the codes and the live data, and ask what the truck was doing when the problem showed up.
We test the suspect parts and systems so the diagnosis is a fact, not a hunch.
We fix the cause, clear the codes and confirm the repair under load.

faqs.q: What is a derate?
faqs.a: A derate is the engine reducing power to protect itself or to limit emissions when it detects a problem, often tied to the aftertreatment system. It's a sign to get the truck checked before it gets worse.

faqs.q: Can a DPF be cleaned instead of replaced?
faqs.a: Depending on its condition, a DPF can sometimes be cleaned rather than replaced. We'll tell you which makes sense after testing.

faqs.q: Do you work on every engine brand?
faqs.a: Ask us about your specific engine. We'll tell you honestly if a job is better handled by a dealer.

services.name: Electrical & Lighting
services.short: Wiring, batteries, alternators, starters, lights and trailer connections, traced to the cause.
services.title: Truck & Trailer Electrical Repair in Garland, TX
services.description: Truck and trailer electrical repair: lights, 7-way plugs, wiring harnesses, batteries, alternators, starters and ABS sensor faults diagnosed and fixed.
services.lead: Dead lights, dying batteries and gremlins in the wiring cost drivers time and tickets. We trace electrical faults to the root cause and fix them properly.
intro: Electrical problems are rarely where they first appear. A trailer light that flickers might be a corroded plug, a bad ground or a chafed wire two feet away. We test the circuit instead of guessing.
Whether it's a single marker light or a no-start, you'll know what failed and why.
included: Headlights, marker, clearance and brake lights
7-way trailer plug, cable and receptacle repair
Battery testing, charging-system checks and replacement
Alternator and starter diagnosis and replacement
signs: Lights flicker or won't come on
Trailer lights work on some trailers but not others
Slow cranking or a dead battery
Fuses keep blowing
The ABS warning light stays on
Gauges or switches act up

steps.d: We check voltage, grounds and connections to find where the fault really is.
We repair or replace the failed part and protect the connection against the next failure.
We check everything works together, including the trailer connection.

faqs.q: Why do my trailer lights keep going out?
faqs.a: The most common culprits are a corroded or damaged 7-way plug, a poor ground connection or a chafed wire. Testing the circuit finds which one.

faqs.q: Do broken lights matter at inspection?
faqs.a: Yes. Lighting devices are among the items listed in Appendix A to 49 CFR Part 396 for the annual inspection, and working lights are also checked at roadside inspections.

faqs.q: Can you fix a no-start on the road?
faqs.a: Often. Dead batteries, loose terminals and failed starters are common roadside calls. See roadside assistance.

services.name: Suspension, Axles & Landing Gear
services.short: Springs, air bags, shocks, bushings, axle parts and landing gear repaired and tested.
services.title: Truck Suspension & Axle Repair in Garland, TX
services.description: Suspension, axle and landing gear repair for tractors and trailers: air springs, leaf springs, bushings, shocks, alignment checks and fifth wheels.
services.lead: Springs, air bags, bushings, axle parts and landing gear take a beating. We repair them so your truck and trailer ride, track and carry the way they should.
intro: Suspension problems rarely announce themselves loudly. They show up as uneven tire wear, a trailer that sits low on one side or a ride that gets rougher month by month.
We inspect the whole load path, from the fifth wheel to the axle ends, and repair what's worn or damaged.
included: Air springs (air bags), leveling valves and air lines
Leaf springs, spring hangers and bushings
Fifth wheel inspection, lubrication and repair
Trailer landing gear repair and replacement
signs: Uneven or rapid tire wear
The trailer sags or sits unevenly
A rough or bouncing ride
The trailer tracks sideways behind the tractor
A leaking air bag, or an air ride that won't hold height
Landing gear that's hard to crank or won't hold

steps.d: We look over springs, bags, bushings, axles, the fifth wheel and the frame.
We show you what's worn, what's urgent and what can wait.
We replace what's needed and check alignment and ride height.

faqs.q: How do I know if trailer axles are out of alignment?
faqs.a: Uneven tire wear and a trailer that tracks slightly sideways behind the tractor are classic signs. An alignment check will confirm it.

faqs.q: Do you repair landing gear?
faqs.a: Yes. Landing gear problems, from seized cranks to damaged legs, are a common trailer repair.

faqs.q: Is suspension part of the DOT inspection?
faqs.a: Yes. Suspension and frame are both listed in Appendix A to 49 CFR Part 396.

services.name: Tires & Wheel Ends
services.short: Tire repair and replacement, mounting, balancing, wheel seals and bearings for tractors and trailers.
services.title: Truck Tire & Wheel-End Service in Garland, TX
services.description: Truck tire repair and replacement, mounting and balancing, plus wheel seals, bearings and hub service for tractors and trailers.
services.lead: Tires and wheel ends decide whether you arrive on time. We repair, replace and inspect them for tractors and trailers.
intro: A tire problem rarely stays small. Underinflation, misalignment and worn wheel-end parts all show up as heat, uneven wear and, eventually, a blowout.
We inspect the whole wheel end, not just the rubber, so the real cause gets fixed.
included: Tire repair and replacement for steer, drive and trailer positions
Tire and wheel inspection for wear, damage and pressure
Hub oil level checks and leak repair
Lug nut and stud checks, and wheel torque
Rim and wheel inspection for cracks and damage
signs: A tire is low, bulging, cut or visibly damaged
Uneven or one-sided tread wear
A vibration at highway speed
Oil leaking from a hub cap or wheel seal
A grinding or rumbling sound from a wheel end
A tire that keeps losing pressure

steps.d: We check tread, sidewalls, pressure, rims and the wheel end.
We show you the damage and recommend repair or replacement.
We repair or replace, balance, and torque the wheels to spec.

faqs.q: Why check tire pressure when the tires are cold?
faqs.a: Tire pressure rises as tires heat up while you drive, so a cold reading is the dependable one. Underinflated tires run hotter and are more likely to fail.

faqs.q: Do you handle roadside tire changes?
faqs.a: Yes. Flats and blowouts are among the most common roadside calls. See roadside assistance.

faqs.q: Can you replace tires while I wait?
faqs.a: For many jobs, yes. Call ahead and we'll tell you what we have and how long it will take.

services.name: Trailer Repair
services.short: Doors, floors, hinges, rear impact guards and landing gear, keeping dry vans and flatbeds road-ready.
services.title: Semi Trailer Repair in Garland, TX
services.description: Trailer repair for dry vans and flatbeds: roll-up and swing doors, floors, panels, rear impact guards, landing gear, lights and flatbed hardware.
services.lead: Doors, floors, lights, landing gear and more. We keep dry vans and flatbeds road-ready and out of the way of delays at the dock.
intro: A trailer that won't close, seal or roll is a trailer that isn't earning. Most trailer problems are straightforward to fix once someone has a good look.
We handle the body, the running gear and the lights, so you drop one trailer and pick up one that's ready to haul.
included: Roll-up and swing door repair: tracks, hinges and latches
Flatbed hardware: winches and tie-down points
signs: A door won't close, latch or seal
Light shows through the roof or sidewall
Soft spots or damage in the floor
A damaged or bent rear impact guard
A winch or tie-down point that's failing
A dock hit or yard accident

steps.d: We inspect the damage and check the running gear while we're there.
You get a clear estimate with the must-fix items separated from the nice-to-have ones.
We fix it, check lights and doors, and hand back a trailer that's ready to roll.

faqs.q: Can you repair damage from a dock hit?
faqs.a: Yes. Door, panel, guard and frame damage from dock and yard accidents is common work.

faqs.q: Do you repair refrigerated trailers?
faqs.a: Refrigeration units are often handled by brand-authorized specialists. Call us about your unit and we'll tell you what we can do and who to see for the rest.

faqs.q: Are trailers part of the annual inspection?
faqs.a: Yes. Trailers are inspected under the same periodic inspection rules as tractors.

services.name: DOT Annual Inspections
services.short: Periodic inspections of your tractor or trailer against federal minimum standards, with a report for your records.
services.title: DOT Annual Truck & Trailer Inspections in Garland, TX
services.description: DOT annual (periodic) inspections for tractors, straight trucks and trailers under 49 CFR Part 396, with repairs and a completed inspection report.
services.lead: Stay compliant without the guesswork. We inspect your tractor or trailer against the federal minimum standards and fix what needs fixing.
intro: Federal rules require every commercial motor vehicle to be inspected at least once every 12 months, and the inspection has to cover, at a minimum, the items listed in Appendix A to 49 CFR Part 396.
We go through each item, tell you what passes and what doesn't, repair what you approve, and give you a completed inspection report for your records.
signs: Your 12-month inspection date is coming up
You've just bought a used tractor or trailer
A roadside inspection flagged a problem
Your carrier or insurer asks for documentation
You're adding a truck to your fleet

steps.d: Call or request service and tell us what you're bringing in. {{appointments}}
We go through every required item and note what passes and what doesn't.
We repair what you approve and give you the completed inspection report.

faqs.q: How often is a DOT annual inspection required?
faqs.a: At least once every 12 months (49 CFR 396.17).

faqs.q: What does the inspection cover?
faqs.a: At minimum, the components listed in Appendix A to Part 396: the brake system, coupling devices, exhaust, fuel system, lighting, safe loading, steering, suspension, frame, tires, wheels and rims, windshield glazing and wipers, and rear impact guards, among others.

faqs.q: Is a roadside inspection the same thing?
faqs.a: No. A roadside inspection is done by an enforcement officer at the roadside. The annual inspection is a separate, periodic inspection of the vehicle.

faqs.q: What should I bring?
faqs.a: Bring the vehicle, any prior inspection reports and a list of problems you've noticed. If something was flagged at a roadside inspection, bring that report too.

services.name: Preventive Maintenance
services.short: Scheduled service with fluids, filters, lubrication and inspections, so small issues don't become breakdowns.
services.title: Truck & Trailer Preventive Maintenance in Garland, TX
services.description: Preventive maintenance for tractors, straight trucks and trailers: oil and filter service, lubrication, inspections and battery, brake and tire checks.
services.lead: The cheapest repair is the one you never need. Scheduled service keeps small issues from becoming breakdowns.
intro: Preventive maintenance is boring on purpose. Fresh fluids, clean filters, greased joints and a careful look at brakes, tires and lights are what keep a truck out of the shop and on the road.
We'll follow your manufacturer's schedule, or help you build one that fits how you actually run.
signs: Service is due by miles, hours or time
You're heading out on a long haul
You've just taken on a used truck or trailer
The season is changing and heat or cold is coming
You'd like predictable maintenance costs

steps.d: We match service intervals to your engine, your duty cycle and the manufacturer's recommendations.
We do the scheduled work and check the items that tend to fail next.
You get notes on what we did and what's coming up, so nothing slips.

faqs.q: How often should I service my truck?
faqs.a: Intervals depend on the engine, how you use the truck and the manufacturer's schedule. We follow yours and can help you set one if you don't have it.

faqs.q: Can you set up a program for my fleet?
faqs.a: Yes. See our fleet services page, or call and tell us about your trucks.

faqs.q: Does maintenance include a safety check?
faqs.a: Yes. Brakes, tires, lights and leaks get checked at each visit so issues are caught early.
